_comment: Does the pipeline notice when a market's date isn't actually in the source posts? `expect_supported` is the ground truth. The hard cases are the last two: a date absent from the posts but genuinely public knowledge (should pass) versus one the model would have to invent (should fail).

cases.name: date stated outright
cases.event: Golden State Warriors vs Los Angeles Lakers, Aug 8 2026
tweets: Lakers at Warriors on August 8, 2026. Curry questionable.

cases.name: relative timing only
cases.event: Golden State Warriors vs Los Angeles Lakers
tweets: Lakers at Warriors tomorrow night, tip-off at 7.

cases.name: no timing information at all
cases.note: The classic invented date — nothing in the posts pins a day.
cases.event: Golden State Warriors vs Los Angeles Lakers, Sep 15 2026
tweets: The Warriors and Lakers rivalry is the best in basketball right now
Curry vs LeBron never gets old honestly

cases.name: posts name a different date
cases.event: Golden State Warriors vs Los Angeles Lakers, Aug 8 2026
tweets: Warriors host the Lakers on September 20, 2026 per the schedule release.

cases.name: speculative event stated as scheduled
cases.event: Apple announces foldable iPhone at October 2026 event
tweets: Rumours swirling that Apple might do a foldable at some point
Would be cool if they announced it this year but who knows

cases.name: invented threshold
tweets: Bitcoin is having a strong year, lots of momentum into Q4

cases.name: fixed public event, date not in posts
cases.note: Hard case the other way: the date is absent from the text but genuinely well known, so the evidence check should let it through.
tweets: Everyone already planning their New Year's Day 2027 resolutions lol
